As of 300 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Gusty showers and isolated thunderstorms are 
possible along a strong cold front tonight into Saturday morning. 
Much cooler with steady light to moderate rain on Saturday.  

Warm and humid weather prevails this afternoon ahead of an 
approaching cold front over the central Appalachians and northern 
Mid-Atlantic. Strong low pressure is tracking east over the St 
Lawrence Valley, with a sharpening upper trough over the mid-MS 
River Valley/Midwest. A broken line of gusty showers and a few tstms 
have developed just ahead of the front from WV to central PA. 
Locally, temperatures are in the lower-mid 80s with mid 60s dew pts. 
Instability is meager with only a few hundred J/kg of MLCAPE. The 
front continues to move SE toward the FA this evening before 
crossing the area tonight. Am still expecting a line of shallow 
convection to cross the area with the front, which is what most of 
the CAMs predict. The most likely timing for tstms is between 7
PM-1 AM. While widespread 30-40 mph gusts are likely with the 
line, the nighttime timing and limited instability (MLCAPE ~500 
J/kg or less) should keep the overall severe threat low for a 
majority of the area. Will need to keep an eye on far 
northeastern portions of the area (MD Eastern Shore) where there
may be slightly better kinematics (though less in the way of 
thermodynamics as sfc heating has been less here). Temps remain 
in the 70s with a quick drop to around 60F shortly after the 
FROPA. 

The front moves well to our southeast Saturday morning while the 
upper trough becomes a closed low as it tracks into western VA. A 
large area of light to moderate rain develops ahead of that trough 
and tracks across the area during the day. Rain likely ends by 
midday inland, but may linger through the late aftn/early evening 
near the coast. Additionally, a secondary, stronger surge of CAA 
will cross the area from mid to late Saturday morning. Therefore, 
Daytime highs will be achieved during the early morning hours, with 
temperatures struggling to get out of the mid 50s by the afternoon 
(and could even fall into the lower 50s where it is raining). So, 24 
hour temperature changes could be in the neighborhood of 30-35+ 
degrees from this afternoon-Saturday afternoon! Deep mixing in the 
wake of the front will promote breezy N winds, with gusts of 25 to 
35+ mph inland and 40 to 50 mph along the immediate coast. A Wind 
Advisory has been issued for VA Beach/Eastern Currituck starting at 
noon Saturday.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Much cooler temperatures arrive this weekend, with 
frost possible Sunday morning, mainly in the Piedmont.

Strong NW flow aloft in the wake of the cold front will usher in the 
coolest airmass of the season Saturday night into Sunday.
Strong sfc high pressure builds east from the OH Valley, but there 
will likely be a decent pressure gradient locally, especially closer 
to the coast. With the surface high forecast to be 1035mb+, kept the 
theme from the previous forecast and undercut NBM lows by a few 
degrees in the northern Piedmont where decoupling is more probable 
closer to sunrise (lows into the mid 30s). Depending on dewpoints, 
at least patchy frost will be possible there. Closer to the coast, 
lows will range from the upper 40s to mid 50s. Mostly sunny Sunday 
(potentially more clouds in the SE) with highs about 10 degrees 
below normal, in the upper 50s to lower 60s. Additional frost 
potential is possible Sunday night into Monday morning across the 
northern Piedmont with temperatures again dropping back into the 
30s. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...There is still some uncertainty for next week 
with a potential strong coastal system lingering offshore or 
retrograding back towards the local area.

There is still a decent amount of uncertainty with respect to the 
track and strength of coastal low pressure late this weekend into 
early next week. Sunday will most likely be dry and cool as the low 
deepens 100-200 miles east of the NC coast while strong high 
pressure wedges down from the north. Guidance continues to struggle 
with how close this coastal system remains to the shoreline, though 
most of the ensemble solutions show the low meandering around 100-
200 miles off the southern VA or NC coast. However, there are still 
hints (especially from the deterministic GFS and Canadian) that it 
could retrograde back towards the local area on Monday before moving 
a bit back out to sea by mid to late week. Precipitation chances 
have increased on Monday (especially near the coast) and have kept 
at least some PoPs in the forecast through much of next week. The 
50th percentile GFS/Canadian Ensemble QPF is 0.25-1.00" across much 
of the area on Monday, though the EPS has noticeably less rain.
